label: Modal spine H2: a metric Grim Reaper with spaced stations, its reach and objection audit
summary: Target: modal spine stage one, horn H2 of the initial-state rival, the next test named by attempt ac336333 (a metric version of the Grim Reaper patchwork argument). Spec: specs/modal-spine-metric-grim-reaper.toml. ENCODING. TruthCore.Causality.MetricGrimReaper adds a TimeClock (a real time coordinate strictly increasing along the order of moments, Mathlib StrictMono), metrically finite pasts (readings at or before t bounded below, Mathlib BddBelow) and spaced descents (every slot at least some fixed delta > 0). The local Reaper pieces and the gluing step are those of GrimReaperPatchwork, restricted to spaced descents below populated moments: two OPEN premises, spaced local pieces (37d4e072) and spaced patchwork (bb7b476c). One clock serves every world of the frame and time is linearly ordered (type-class assumption); a world-indexed clock is not built. RESULTS. populatedPastsMetricallyFiniteOfPatchwork (f5ede5eb): in every accessible history every populated moment has a metrically finite past (4365c3c5). In linear time a metrically infinite past has a spaced descent by a theorem (spacedDescentOfUnbounded); no separate countable-coinitiality premise appears, but a real clock exists only for orders embedding in the reals, so countable coinitiality is absorbed into the clock's existence, not eliminated (times with no real clock, such as reverse omega_1, the long line or lexicographic R x R, are outside the scope); the proof composes GrimReaperPatchwork.arrangementImpossible and hence IndexedSignalReaper.impossible, without restating them. Strength orders: coinitial pieces and patchwork strengthen the spaced ones (535d5cb8, 296c3904; a spaced descent is coinitial in linear time); control 2 shows the pieces order strict (silent registers) and the two premises jointly strict, while strictness of the patchwork order alone is not checked. Begun populated pasts strengthen metrically finite ones (3f6bddb7), strictly by control 2, so founded => begun => metrically finite. Controls (83fd4e6f): (1) in the beginningless integer history each spaced premise holds without the other and populated pasts are not metrically finite; (2) positive real times (open below, finite: the order and metric shape of FLRW cosmic time): for every register frame both spaced premises hold and the coinitial ones do not both hold, and with silent registers coinitial local pieces fail; populated pasts metrically finite and not begun; with A3 prime b (6dd276f0) holding, A3 prime w (6d71688e) fails; (3) non-negative real times, nothing present at 0: for every register frame both spaced premises hold and the unrestricted ones do not both hold; populated pasts begun, not founded; begun coming-to-be possible. REACH. The conclusion is that no populated past is metrically infinite, not that populated pasts are begun. CLOCK. Metric finiteness is not invariant under reparametrization (arctan makes integer pasts finite; ln t makes FLRW pasts infinite). Disambiguation 725f3417 (CLOCK) separates CLOCK_1, the physically privileged duration (cosmic or proper time; PrivilegedClock, an explicit primitive marker), from CLOCK_2, any order-preserving real coordinate (TimeClock). The theorems hold for every CLOCK_2; statements and verdicts are read with CLOCK_1. Why duration should matter: on the spatiotemporal route of the #367 audit (a possible isolated Placer, regions large enough for the mechanism, infinitary spatiotemporal patchwork, intrinsic powers), stations are duplicates of one patch, and a duplicate keeps its intrinsic (proper) duration; room for infinitely many duplicates of a patch lasting at most delta is exactly a descent with slots of at least delta. OBJECTION AUDIT (Substantive Objection Standard; repaired after the independent semantic challenge). Undercutting objection to the warrant of spaced patchwork, kept conditional on L (solutions of accepted laws are metaphysically possible) or C: recombination, the only warrant on file, is blind to durations; spaced and accumulating descents carry the same pieces in order-isomorphic positions, so it warrants the coinitial and unrestricted instances equally, which exclude a populated FLRW past (control 2) and, given C, first-moment continua (control 3). Answered only by a duration-sensitive principle, recombination of duplicates of one possible patch, room permitting, which warrants spaced arrangements only; its countable generalization is presented as plausible, not derived (#367 audit), and its bridge to the typed premise is not built. Misner-type logarithmic time (lead from memory, not read: Misner 1969, Absolute Zero of Time): kept as an open objection to the clock choice; under ln t the FLRW objection returns; reply: proper time is what ideal clocks measure and what duplication preserves; unresolved whether station patches near the singularity can keep a fixed proper duration. FLRW: no target, read with CLOCK_1 (spaced descents exist only below metrically infinite pasts; control 2); it still applies to begun populated pasts and to any bridge from metric finiteness to begun pasts. Benardete parity: no target (no spaced descent in [0, t] or (0, t]; controls 2, 3); its transfer to metrically infinite pasts remains an unsupported suggestion (needs the diagnosis that gluing fails for every infinite descending arrangement; no independent reason recorded). Rebutting objection, kept conditional on L (labelled like the FLRW row, which rests on the same principle): accepted theories have populated solutions with a metrically infinite past (Einstein static universe in general relativity; eternal free motion in Newtonian mechanics); if every solution of accepted laws is a possible history the conclusion fails. Established: these are solutions. Not established: that being a solution suffices for metaphysical possibility, the same principle the FLRW row relies on. It names no failing piece or gluing step; since an infinite past is the Reaper's intended target, it sets law-consistency as a guide to possibility directly against recombination; its weight is that comparison, not resolved. Global-compatibility reply: unchanged fork (overlapAgreeingWitnessesImpossible holds for every descent; on the value-agreement reading the argument does not start; on the duplication reading no acyclic gluing failure along a non-accumulating descent is recorded). Unsatisfiable-pair diagnosis: no mechanism. One clock and linear time: encoding scope, no mechanism of failure identified. Plain verdict: read with CLOCK_1 the typed premises' scope excludes metrically finite pasts; the warrant is unchanged: duration-blind recombination, the only warrant on file (#367 audit, defeasible), supports the refuted instances equally (undercutting objection kept), unless the duration-sensitive duplication principle is adopted; the clock choice faces the open Misner-type objection; one rebutting objection is kept conditional on L. CONNECTION. The A3 prime w derivation (possiblyBegunOfEarlierGrounds) needs begun populated pasts; control 2 shows metric finiteness with A3 prime b does not give A3 prime w. Plans, not built: (1) a named open bridge, every populated moment with a metrically finite past has a begun past, which is exactly what FLRW denies, so the FLRW cost is isolated in that bridge rather than removed (the composition would be a transcription step and is not registered); (2) a metric arrival replacing the empty-moment step (A2 with A3), blocked because an open-below finite populated past has no empty moment and no such arrival premise is formulated. Nothing is attributed to Koons or Pruss. No premise is established.
blocker: Both spaced premises are OPEN; their only recorded support is the general, duration-blind recombination principle, which is undercut as a warrant for them unless a duration-sensitive duplication principle (room permitting) is adopted and its countable generalization defended. The clock choice (CLOCK_1) is open against Misner-type logarithmic time (lead, not read). The metric conclusion reaches A3 prime w only through an open bridge from metrically finite to begun populated pasts, which the FLRW objection targets directly. Next tests: weigh that bridge against FLRW, or formulate a metric arrival needing no empty moment; compare the warrant of law-consistency as a guide to possibility with recombination; a world-indexed clock if frames with differing metrics are needed.
